what: The words of the guide: for each step and each state inside it, the objective, what the guide says, the labels on things, the actions, and the questions a visitor can ask. Every sentence says which of the five places it sits in. Text in braces is a field: its value comes from an answer of the backend, named under fields. No figure is typed in a line.

score.is: On each pass of the sharp satellite, take every square that the estimate or the satellite marks as burning. Agreement is the share of those squares, over all its passes, that both mark.
score.written: the level in percent, a change in points; one point is one percent
score.in_the_answers: the round serves it as score, score_start and score_end under the name csi; a run serves the same measure as csi_strict_375m

time.rule: Every line gives local time at the fire, with the day and the part of the day. UTC is written only in the document viewer.
time.how: One format, local_day_time, from the instant and the middle longitude of the fire's box. A decimal hour that an answer serves rounded is never used: cutting it to minutes can show the minute before.
time.kind: It is time by the sun at the fire, not the civil clock of its time zone, which can stand an hour or more away. Method and Data says so.

places_for_words.objective: place 1, top left, one line: what the visitor is doing now. The trail and the context line sit with it.
places_for_words.guide: place 2, bottom centre: the one or two sentences of a state that stand together and stay. A question's answer and a state's more lines are said here on demand, and the standing sentences return. The results rows of a round's end stand above it as part of what it says.
places_for_words.label: place 3, joined to one thing on the stage by a thin leader: one or two short sentences about that thing.
places_for_words.prompt: place 4, beside the thing it acts on, with its key, only while the pointer or the keyboard's focus is on or near that thing. A start card is a prompt opened out.
places_for_words.sheet: place 5, on demand only: the document viewer from the side, whose words are in SHEETS-copy.json, and the key of marks, whose rows are under marks. UTC is written only in the document viewer.

reading.place: Every sentence carries place: objective, guide, label, prompt or sheet, as places_for_words says them. A sentence about one thing is at that thing; a sentence about the whole step is in the guide.
reading.objective: Every state has one: a verb phrase for what the visitor does, with no full stop. A step's own objective is that of its main state.
reading.context: A step's context is the fainter line that goes with the objective: the place and the days. It stands under the objective or beside the trail, never above it. It is not a sentence.
reading.says: The one or two sentences that stand at rest. They are shown together and stay; nothing passes by in turn. Each item is one sentence that can be read alone, with place, line and sometimes if or unless. Whatever the conditions, at least one stands and never more than two. A state may hold more items than two when their conditions exclude each other; whatever the conditions, one or two stand.
reading.says_if: A line with an if is shown only when the named condition is true; with unless, only when it is false.
reading.labels: Each has on, a thing named under things, and a line. A label with if or unless follows the same rule as a line. short, where present, is the label while the passes play: it must be readable in a second and a half.
reading.actions: At most three, the next step first; the first is the only strong one. places says where an action is offered: the guide strip always, and a prompt beside the thing that beside names, shown only while the pointer or the keyboard's focus is on or near that thing. label_while_on, where present, is what the action reads while what it started is running.
reading.start_card: A step's first screen may open its prompt into a small card at the thing named by at: the step's name, the line do, the line done, and the key of the state's first action. It folds back once the visitor acts.
reading.results: At a round's end: rows. Each row has a name, a field written with the unit, sometimes a note; a note with note_if is shown only when that condition is true.
reading.fields: route and key say where the value is. format says how to write it. A key with a comma is several values the format takes together. A line whose field has no value is not shown, and no stand-in number is.
reading.questions: ask is the question as the picker shows it. match holds words and phrases; a typed question is matched on them. answer is what the guide says. command, when present, is carried out as well. where lists the steps in which the picker offers it; it can be asked anywhere.
reading.keys with words: A key such as frames[last coarse before pass] is a rule in words: the last pass before the one on show that is the coarse satellite's and has a detection in the box. records[fire month] is the record of the month of the fire the page opens on.
reading.time: See time. Every instant in a line is written with the format local_day_time.
reading.more: What the guide says on demand in that state, beyond what stands: when the visitor asks to be told more (the command say:more). A state's on_demand questions are the other way to more.
reading.also: A step's also lists actions that work in every state of the step, by their key and by asking, and are not in the guide strip unless a state lists them.
reading.marks: The key of marks, on demand. Each row has a name and a line for one mark, when it is on show, the served field it is drawn from, what of it is drawing, and where that was stated. action is the one action that shows the squares sized by chance.
reading.exclusive: Groups of conditions of which at most one is true at a time, read from the same answer; the check of what stands counts no case where two of a group hold.

things.fire: the fire on the land, in a round as well
things.frames: the white frames of the estimate, which lie on the fire; their label may hang on the fire's leader as its second line
things.month: the month the visitor picked in the record
things.fire_month: the month of the fire the page opens on, marked in the record
things.marked_square: the square a look would go to: under the pointer, or chosen with the keyboard
things.looked_square: the square the visitor just looked at
things.side_block: one of the three small terrains, when the fire is shown side by side
things.dotted_line: the dotted line around the ground where the model gives fire a chance
things.learned_block: the Learned Player's small terrain, when the players stand side by side
things.fire_block: one fire's block on the choice of a place

formats.count: a whole number with a comma for thousands
formats.count_word: zero to twelve as a word, larger numbers as digits
formats.length: the number of items of a list, written as count_word
formats.percent: the value times 100, rounded to a whole number
formats.points: the value times 100, one decimal place, with a plus or minus sign: points of agreement
formats.percent1: the value times 100, one decimal place: percent of agreement
formats.count_none: a whole number, zero written as none
formats.year: the first four characters of a month or an instant
formats.month_year: month name and year, from a year and month
formats.list_and: the items with commas and a final and
formats.mean_points: the mean of a list, written as points
formats.ordinal: the value plus one, because the answer counts from zero
formats.said_as: the served word replaced by the phrase the field gives for it under said_as
formats.length_digits: the number of items of a list, in digits
formats.local_day_time: the day, the month, the time and the part of the day at the fire, such as 11 August, 1:11 at night. Take the instant, add the middle longitude of the fire's box divided by fifteen, in hours, and cut to the minute without rounding. Write the hour on a twelve-hour clock, then the part of the day: in the morning from 5:00, in the afternoon from 12:00, in the evening from 18:00, at night from 21:00 until 5:00. One function for every line, never a decimal hour that was rounded.
formats.local_day_range: the days of two instants, each moved to local time as local_day_time does, as one range, such as 9 to 12 August 2012
formats.ratio_whole: the first value divided by the second, rounded to a whole number; no value when the second is zero
formats.month_name: the name of the month of the year, such as August
formats.count_keys_with_fires: the number of keys whose episodes are more than zero, written as count_word
formats.score_names_ahead: the scores whose class is ahead, each by its phrase under score_names, as list_and
formats.score_names_behind: the scores whose class is behind, each by its phrase under score_names, as list_and
formats.count_no: zero written as no, one to twelve as words, larger numbers as digits

learned_trained_here.true_when: episode.split is fit: the round is one of those the Learned Player was trained on

not_always_ahead.true_when: the smallest of test_fires.fires[].new.ahead_of_both_on is less than scores_judged

fire_month_stands_out.true_when: records[fire month].harmonized_mean divided by records[fire month].month_median is at least two and under a hundred, and that median is above zero

this_month_is_counted.true_when: the answer holds a rate for the days counted and no error

players_from_round.true_when: from is round: the blocks are the round the visitor just played, not plays asked on the open fire
players_from_round.route: the page: usePlayersView() of the players' picture

method_replaced.true_when: harmonization_method.id is not overlap_ratio_v1: the Record serves the method the harmonize lane's rule chose

test_a_strict_not_behind.true_when: fresh_test.test_a is not null and its csi_strict_375m is not behind

state_when.recorded_test_fire: the run's answer has not_scored (POST /api/reconstruct), or places[id].featured_fires[fire].closed is true (GET /api/regions)
state_when.no_sharp_satellite: the month is before regime_markers[label begins VIIRS].year_month (GET /api/calendar)
state_when.no_fire_to_rebuild: no start of real_run_starts.starts lies in the month (GET /api/calendar)
state_when.own_area: place.kind is not region (GET /api/calendar with a box)
state_when.looks_spent: observation.budget_left is zero and done is false (POST /api/env/next_look/step)
state_when.as_counted: the visitor asked to see the years as counted (record:as_counted is on)
state_when.this_month: the visitor asked for this month so far (record:now); GET /api/calendar/current has answered or failed
state_when.players_open: the players' picture is ready and what the looks found can still be revealed (usePlayersView: state ready, canReveal true)
state_when.players_found: the players' picture is ready and what the looks found is drawn (state ready, foundShown true)
state_when.players_held: the players' picture is asked for while a round is under way (state held)
state_when.players_coming: the plays are still coming (state loading)
state_when.players_failed: the plays did not load (state failed)
state_when.place: the choice of a place is open; it opens only when asked for (P, or the place's name beside the trail), and Escape returns to where it was opened from

commands.go:record: open the fire record over the stage
commands.go:estimate: close what is open and show the fire with the sharp satellite hidden
commands.go:test: reveal what the sharp satellite saw; asked on a pass of the coarse satellite, move first to the nearest pass of the sharp satellite (the next one, else the one before)
commands.go:play: start a round on this fire
commands.place:draw: let the visitor draw an area on the map
commands.record:pick: let the visitor pick a month in the grid
commands.record:default_fire: mark the default fire's month in the grid
commands.record:accuracy: annotate the record with the left-out-year check
commands.record:csv: give the picked month's detections as a CSV file
commands.passes:play: play the passes in order, each held about a second and a half, the fire's label in its short form; the same key and the same action pause them, and while they play the action reads label_while_on
commands.passes:hidden_next: go to the next hidden pass
commands.play:look: spend a look on the marked square
commands.play:skip: let this pass go by without a look
commands.play:players: show the other players side by side: their looks, gains and lines; what the looks found only once seen or asked for
commands.play:watch: play the other players' looks in order
commands.close: close what is open, or leave the round, and return to the fire as it was before
commands.play:end: let the passes that are left go by without a look and end the round
commands.say:more: say the state's more lines in the guide, one after another at the reader's pace, then let the standing sentences return; where a state has none, offer its on_demand questions
commands.record:as_counted: draw the years as the satellites counted them, before the correction; the same action goes back to one scale
commands.record:now: ask for this month so far and mark it as the record's next square
commands.record:now_caveats: list why this month's figure is rough, in the sentences the route serves under caveats
commands.marks:key: open or close the key of marks: one row for each mark now on show
commands.estimate:chance: draw the squares sized by the chance of fire, which are off at rest; the same action hides them
commands.play:players_reveal: draw what the players' looks found, which is the hidden satellite's; offered only while the picture says it can be asked (canReveal)
commands.play:resume: close the players' picture and go back to the round under way
commands.place:choose: open the fire record of the marked fire's place, with that fire marked; the marked fire has the keyboard's focus when the choice opens

says.line: What you saw: one fair fire record across two kinds of satellite, an estimate tested with the sharp satellite hidden, and a game for choosing where to look next.
The same test can be put to any two instruments that watched the same thing; here it is done for one pair.

steps.objective: Try another fire or your own area

answer.line: One light is one square of ground where a satellite saw the heat of fire as it passed. It is a reading from orbit, not a flame.
Two kinds of NASA instrument that spot fires from orbit by their heat. MODIS, the coarse one, is on record here since {record_first_year}; VIIRS, the sharp one, since {sharp_since}.

The sharp satellite sees smaller squares of ground, so it catches small and cool fires the coarse ones miss. Around {place} it has about {sharp_to_coarse} times as many detections in the years both flew.

questions.ask: What is the fire record for?

answer.line: It lets you compare any month or year with any other since {record_first_year}, although the satellites changed on the way. That is what was asked for: one record across both kinds of satellite.

questions.ask: How well does the correction hold?

answer.line: Hide one year and predict it from the others: in a typical year the prediction is off by {record_error} percent.
Without the correction for the change of satellite it is off by {record_error_raw} percent.
Yes. Pick a month and take its detections as a table, as NASA's fire service lists them.
These are the places and fires you can open.

questions.ask: Can I use my own area?

answer.line: You can draw an area and get its fire record. A fire can be shown pass by pass and tested only where the satellites' passes are stored: {places_with_fires}.
Each white frame is one square, {sharp_square_m} metres across, that the model says is burning at that moment. Together they are its estimate of what the sharp satellite would see.

questions.ask: What did the model get to see?

answer.line: {coarse_passes} passes of the coarse satellite with {coarse_detections} detections, and the shape of the ground. Nothing from the sharp satellite.

questions.ask: How do I know it did not peek?

answer.line: The sharp satellite's detections are set apart before the estimate is made and are opened only to score it. Delete them and the estimate comes out the same, and a test checks that.
The sharp satellite is hidden again.

The estimate and {simple_methods_n} simple methods are each compared with what the sharp satellite saw, in {scores_n} ways. On {ahead_on} of them the estimate did better than every simple method, by plain comparison of the numbers.
One takes the coarse satellite's squares as the fire. The other does the same and scales the amount by how much more the sharp satellite usually sees.
No. On the {test_fires_n} fires kept as its test it beat the simple methods on {test_fire_scores} of {test_scores_n} scores.
No. On {test_a_fires_n} fires it had never seen it was ahead on {test_a_ahead} of {test_scores_n} scores and behind on {test_a_behind}.

On {other_fires_n} fires of other years, counting a score only when the gap is too large to be luck, it was ahead on {other_ahead} of the {test_scores_n} scores, level on {other_level} and behind on {other_behind}.

questions.ask: Why is the model called experimental?

answer.line: Because on {other_fires_n} fires it had never seen, it was ahead by more than luck on only {other_ahead} of {test_scores_n} scores. That is not enough to switch it on, so it is shown with its tests and nothing more is claimed.

With each estimate the model states an upper limit for how much fire the sharp satellite will see. On this fire the real amount stayed under it on {limit_held} of {limit_of} hidden passes; on other fires, on {other_limit_held} of {other_limit_of}.

questions.ask: Why can't I test this fire?

answer.line: It is one of the {test_fires_n} fires never used to tune the model and kept as its test. Their results are on record and they are not run again, so nothing can be tuned to them.
The page opens on the largest fire the model had never seen, so the test you watch is one it could not have learned.
You chose it. To the model this is {fire_to_model}.

Agreement is how far the estimate and the sharp satellite mark the same squares as burning. On each of its passes, take every square that either marks: agreement is the share of those squares that both mark.
Ground that neither marks is left out, so empty land cannot raise it. A point is one percent of those squares.
A look shows the model what the sharp satellite saw in one square on one pass. It is scored by the points it adds to the estimate's agreement with the sharp satellite, over the whole round.
Part of a look's gain is the looked square itself, which the model then knows. The rest is what the look taught it about other squares.
A simple rule works: look where the model is least sure.
Over {rounds_n} other rounds, each a few days of one fire of other years, it gained more than random looks on {rule_ahead_rounds} of them.
Chance looks at random squares, Follow the Coarse Satellite looks where that satellite last saw fire, and Look Where Unsure looks where the model is least sure.
The Learned Player learned its choices from past fires, and Sees the Answer is not a fair player: it reads the hidden detections.

questions.ask: Does the learned player beat the simple rule?

answer.line: No: over {rounds_n} rounds it had never played, its gain differed from the rule's by {learned_minus_rule} points on average, most likely between {learned_low} and {learned_high}. That is too close to call.
On the rounds measured, yes: over {rounds_n} rounds it had never played, it gained {learned_minus_rule} points more on average, most likely between {learned_low} and {learned_high}.

questions.ask: What is the best anyone could do?

answer.line: One more player is allowed to see the answer and takes the best square at evenly spaced passes: {answer_gain} points on this round. A player that also chooses when to look can do better than it.
The record lists detections, not the places a satellite looked and saw nothing. So an empty pass may be cloud, and the model treats it as unknown.
The detections are NASA's public fire record, FIRMS. The ground is real elevation and imagery, and every source is listed under Method and Data.

questions.ask: What could this be used for?

answer.line: A fair record shows whether a place is burning more than it used to. The same test, with one instrument hidden, can be put to any two that watched the same thing; here it is done for one pair.

no_answer.says: I do not have an answer to that. I can show another fire, explain the two satellites, or explain what you are looking at.
